fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from both directions on the road.
• Install a reflective address marker at the base of the driveway to guide responders arriving at night or in low visibility.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so emergency apparatus can reach the main residence and detached structure without obstruction.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain clearance for fire apparatus and taller emergency vehicles on both sides and overhead.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the detached structure to allow responders to move around all sides of the building.
• Mark or post the address or a unit identifier on the detached structure so responders can distinguish it from the main residence during an emergency.
• Keep a gate, door, or opening in the perimeter fencing at the rear of the property unlocked or equipped with a breakaway latch to allow responders to reach the rear without returning to the front.
• Identify and mark any secondary access point through the perimeter fencing that responders could use if the primary access drive is blocked.
• Clear a walking path along at least one side of the main residence connecting the front to the rear so responders are not forced to push through dense vegetation to reach the back of the property.
• Notify your local fire department of the single access point and detached structure layout so they can note it in pre-incident planning records

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches and shrubs that are directly touching or overhanging the roof and exterior walls of the structure.
• Remove or thin shrubs and low-growing plants immediately around the base of the house to create open ground directly next to the foundation.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure so individual trees are not touching each other with their branches.
• Remove dead branches from the lower trunks of trees surrounding the house, starting with those closest to the structure.
• Thin scattered trees between the tree clusters and the house to break up the continuous path of vegetation leading toward the structure.
• Keep the driveway clear of overhanging branches from the tree line on both sides for its full length.
• Trim back any shrubs or low branches along the driveway edges that narrow the travel lane or reduce visibility.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible to emergency vehicles approaching from the road.
• Keep a turnaround area near the structure clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and stored materials so emergency vehicles can turn around.
• Remove any wood piles, stored materials, or other flammable items that are sitting directly against or within a few feet of the house exterior.
• Mow or cut down tall dry grass in the open green space areas that connect directly to the tree clusters or to the structure.
